paragraphs.paragraph: Jehu the son of Hanani tells Baasha that although the Lord raised him from the dust to become prince over Israel, he followed Jeroboam's sinful way. Therefore Baasha's house will be destroyed as Jeroboam's house was destroyed.
paragraphs.title: The Prophecy Against Baasha's House

easy.explanation: The word of the Lord came to Baasha by Jehu the son of Hanani.
easy.q: Who delivered the word of the Lord to Baasha?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I exalted thee out of the dust.”
easy.q: From what did the Lord say He had exalted Baasha?

easy.explanation: Baasha walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused Israel to sin.

answers: It would reign for many years
medium.explanation: The Lord said He would take away the posterity of Baasha and his house.
medium.q: What judgment was pronounced against Baasha's house?

medium.explanation: The Lord said, “I will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam.”
medium.q: To which house would Baasha's house be made like?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to removing and destroying Baasha's family line.
medium.q: In the KJV context, what does “take away the posterity” mean?

answers: To emphasize the favor he received and his responsibility
To explain why he moved to Samaria
challenge.explanation: Baasha had been raised to power, yet he chose to sin.
challenge.q: Why does the prophecy mention that Baasha was exalted from the dust before describing his sin?

answers: He built a city, so he lost it
He destroyed Jeroboam's house, and his own house would be destroyed
He appointed Jehu, so he was punished
challenge.explanation: Baasha's judgment corresponded to his destruction of Jeroboam's house.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between Baasha's deeds and his judgment?

answers: Dishonor and severe judgment after death
challenge.explanation: The image shows the disgrace and severity of the judgment against Baasha's house.
challenge.q: What do the dogs and birds eating the dead signify?

paragraphs.idea: Jehu the son of Hanani tells Baasha that although the Lord raised him from the dust to become prince over Israel, he followed Jeroboam's sinful way. Therefore Baasha's house will be destroyed as Jeroboam's house was destroyed.

paragraphs.paragraph: Elah reigns briefly, and Zimri, captain of half the chariots, conspires against him and kills him. Zimri destroys all the house of Baasha, fulfilling Jehu's prophecy, but he also continues in the sins of Jeroboam.
paragraphs.title: Elah and Zimri: The Fall of Baasha's House

easy.explanation: Elah was Baasha's son and reigned in his stead.
Zimri went in and smote Elah, and killed him.
The KJV calls Zimri “captain of half his chariots.”

answers: He slew all the house of Baasha
medium.explanation: Zimri left no surviving member of Baasha's household.
medium.q: What did Zimri do after killing Elah?

answers: Elah was worshipping in the temple
Elah was drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza
Elah was with the army at Gibbethon
medium.explanation: Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in Arza's house.
medium.q: What opportunity allowed Zimri to attack Elah?

medium.explanation: Zimri secretly plotted against Elah and overthrew him.
medium.q: What does “conspired against him” mean?

answers: It fulfilled the destruction of Baasha's house
It transferred the prophecy to Judah
challenge.explanation: Zimri destroyed Baasha's house according to the word spoken by Jehu.
challenge.q: How is Zimri's action connected with Jehu's prophecy?

answers: He also sinned and walked in Jeroboam's way
He did not reign in Tirzah
challenge.explanation: The passage condemns Zimri for his own sins and for making Israel sin.
challenge.q: Why is Zimri not presented as a righteous ruler even though he fulfilled the prophecy?

answers: The people had lost interest in kingship
The government was marked by coups and instability
challenge.explanation: Elah was quickly killed and Zimri seized the throne.
challenge.q: What does the rapid change from Elah to Zimri suggest?

paragraphs.idea: Elah reigns briefly, and Zimri, captain of half the chariots, conspires against him and kills him. Zimri destroys all the house of Baasha, fulfilling Jehu's prophecy, but he also continues in the sins of Jeroboam.

paragraphs.paragraph: Zimri reigns for only seven days. The army at Gibbethon makes Omri king, besieges Tirzah, and Zimri burns the king's house around himself and dies. His reign is condemned because he followed the way of Jeroboam.
paragraphs.title: Zimri's Reign and the Army's Revolt

easy.explanation: Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah.
All Israel made Omri, captain of the host, king.
easy.q: Whom did the people make king?

answers: He burned the king's house over himself and died
easy.explanation: Zimri entered the palace, burned it, and died.
easy.q: What did Zimri do when the city was taken?

medium.explanation: The people were encamped at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
medium.q: Where was the army when it made Omri king?

answers: He went up with Israel and besieged Tirzah
He built an altar to Baal
medium.explanation: Omri went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
medium.q: What did Omri do after being made king?

answers: The city fell to the enemy
medium.explanation: Tirzah had been captured by Omri and his forces.
medium.q: In this context, what does “the city was taken” mean?

answers: They heard that Zimri had conspired and killed the king
Jehu commanded them to do so
challenge.explanation: The army heard of Zimri's treason and killing of Elah, so it made Omri king.
challenge.q: Why did the people make Omri king?

answers: He chose to die with the royal palace rather than fall to his enemies
He wanted to build a new palace
challenge.explanation: After the city was taken, Zimri chose death rather than capture.
challenge.q: What is the significance of Zimri burning the palace around himself?

answers: Every king returned to the worship of the Lord
Every king ruled for a long time
Kings sinned and continued in Jeroboam's way
challenge.explanation: Zimri too is judged for walking in Jeroboam's sinful way.
challenge.q: What repeated pattern appears in the judgment of Israel's kings?

paragraphs.idea: Zimri reigns for only seven days. The army at Gibbethon makes Omri king, besieges Tirzah, and Zimri burns the king's house around himself and dies. His reign is condemned because he followed the way of Jeroboam.

paragraphs.paragraph: After Zimri's death, Israel is divided between the followers of Tibni and the followers of Omri. Omri's supporters prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns.
paragraphs.title: The Struggle Between Omri and Tibni

easy.explanation: Half the people followed Tibni and half followed Omri.
The people who followed Omri prevailed.
The passage says, “so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.”

medium.explanation: After Omri's faction prevailed, Omri reigned.
medium.q: What was the result of Omri's supporters prevailing?

answers: A struggle over who would be king
The building of a new city
medium.explanation: The people divided between two rival claimants to the throne.
medium.q: What caused the division of the people?

medium.explanation: Omri's followers prevailed, meaning they defeated Tibni's supporters.
medium.q: What does “prevailed” mean in this passage?

answers: The monarchy was involved in an internal power struggle
The people were united behind Omri
The identity of the king did not matter
challenge.explanation: The division reveals conflict over succession and rule.
challenge.q: What does the division into two groups show?

answers: Omri reigned, Tibni died, then the people divided
The people divided, Tibni died, then Omri reigned
Tibni died, Zimri reigned, then the people divided
challenge.explanation: Israel first divided, then Tibni died, and afterward Omri reigned.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: He received the throne after a struggle
He inherited it immediately from his father
challenge.explanation: Omri became king after his faction overcame Tibni's faction.
challenge.q: What conclusion about Omri's rule is supported by the passage?

paragraphs.idea: After Zimri's death, Israel is divided between the followers of Tibni and the followers of Omri. Omri's supporters prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns.

paragraphs.paragraph: Omri reigns for twelve years, purchases the hill of Samaria, and builds a new capital there. Although he is a strong ruler and builder, he does evil in the eyes of the Lord, worse than all who came before him.
paragraphs.title: Omri Establishes Samaria

easy.explanation: Omri reigned over Israel twelve years.
easy.q: How many years did Omri reign over Israel?

easy.explanation: Omri bought the hill Samaria from Shemer.
Omri named the city after Shemer, the owner of the hill.
easy.q: After whom was the city of Samaria named?

answers: He built a city on it
He gave it to the Philistines
medium.explanation: Omri built the city of Samaria on the hill.
medium.q: What did Omri do after buying the hill?

answers: He did better than all his predecessors
He did worse than all who were before him
Nothing is said about his conduct
medium.explanation: The KJV says Omri “did worse than all that were before him.”
medium.q: How is Omri described morally?

answers: The central city of a kingdom
medium.explanation: Samaria became Omri's central royal city.
medium.q: What is a capital city?

answers: He built a royal center but was judged as sinful
He was a prophet but never spoke
He ruled Judah but built in Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage presents his political achievement alongside his evil conduct.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the description of Omri?

answers: The city was established at a chosen and legally acquired site
The city was immediately captured from the Philistines
The city was built on the land of Jericho
challenge.explanation: The account specifically records the purchase of the hill and construction upon it.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Omri purchasing the hill and building there?

answers: He bought the hill, built a city, and called it Samaria
He named the city, bought the hill, and destroyed it
He built Jericho, bought the hill, and moved to Tirzah
challenge.explanation: This is the order given in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Omri's actions?

paragraphs.idea: Omri reigns for twelve years, purchases the hill of Samaria, and builds a new capital there. Although he is a strong ruler and builder, he does evil in the eyes of the Lord, worse than all who came before him.

paragraphs.paragraph: Ahab reigns in Samaria and does more evil than all the kings before him. He marries Jezebel, serves and worships Baal, builds an altar for Baal, and makes a grove, provoking the Lord to anger.
paragraphs.title: Ahab and the Worship of Baal

easy.explanation: Ahab was the son of Omri.
Ahab took Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, to wife.
easy.q: Whom did Ahab take to wife?

easy.explanation: Ahab reared up an altar for Baal in Samaria.
easy.q: For whom did Ahab build an altar?

answers: He did less evil than all of them
He did evil above all who were before him
medium.explanation: The passage says Ahab did evil above all that were before him.
medium.q: How is Ahab's sin compared with that of earlier kings?

answers: He built an altar for Baal
medium.explanation: Ahab built a house of Baal and an altar for Baal in Samaria.
medium.q: What did Ahab do in connection with Baal worship?

answers: Something he considered easy or insignificant
That he moved to another city
medium.explanation: Ahab regarded walking in Jeroboam's sins as a small matter.
medium.q: What does “a light thing for him” mean in the KJV passage?

answers: Baal worship was brought into the royal center of Israel
All altars in Israel were removed
The people returned to worshipping the Lord
challenge.explanation: Ahab served Baal and built a house and altar for him in Samaria.
challenge.q: What was the main religious result of Ahab's marriage to Jezebel?

answers: He continued Jeroboam's sins and added the worship of Baal and the grove
He transferred the kingdom to Judah
challenge.explanation: Ahab followed Jeroboam's way and promoted Baal worship and a grove.
challenge.q: How did Ahab add to the sins of earlier kings?

answers: Ahab built a house and altar for Baal
Ahab was the son of Omri
challenge.explanation: Building a house and altar established Baal worship publicly.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Baal worship was not merely private?

paragraphs.idea: Ahab reigns in Samaria and does more evil than all the kings before him. He marries Jezebel, serves and worships Baal, builds an altar for Baal, and makes a grove, provoking the Lord to anger.

paragraphs.paragraph: In Ahab's days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilds Jericho. Abiram dies when the foundation is laid, and Segub dies when the gates are set up, according to the word of the Lord spoken by Joshua.
paragraphs.title: The Rebuilding of Jericho and Fulfillment of the Curse

easy.explanation: Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho.
The passage says, “In his days,” referring to Ahab's days.

answers: One died when the foundation was laid and one when the gates were set up
easy.explanation: Abiram died at the foundation, and Segub died when the gates were set up.

medium.explanation: The KJV calls him “Hiel the Bethelite.”
medium.q: What place was Hiel associated with?

answers: When the gates were set up
medium.explanation: Abiram, Hiel's firstborn, died when Hiel laid the foundation.
medium.q: When did Abiram die?

answers: Began the building by setting its base
medium.explanation: To lay a foundation means to begin construction by establishing its base.
medium.q: What does “laid the foundation” mean?

answers: Their deaths fulfilled the word spoken by Joshua
challenge.explanation: The verse ends by saying it happened according to the word spoken by Joshua.
challenge.q: What connection does the verse make between the deaths of Hiel's sons and the word of the Lord?

answers: Segub died at the foundation and Abiram at the gates
Abiram died at the foundation and Segub at the gates
challenge.explanation: Abiram was the firstborn and died at the foundation; Segub died at the gates.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the deaths?

answers: To show when the rebuilding occurred
To say that Ahab personally rebuilt Jericho
To identify Hiel as king of Israel
challenge.explanation: The phrase places Hiel's rebuilding of Jericho during Ahab's reign.
challenge.q: Why does the verse mention Ahab's days?

paragraphs.idea: In Ahab's days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilds Jericho. Abiram dies when the foundation is laid, and Segub dies when the gates are set up, according to the word of the Lord spoken by Joshua.
